name: Restaurants & Food Service
summary: Reservations, waitlists, review management, inventory reorders, and staff scheduling.

automations.title: Online Review Response & Reputation Management System
automations.summary: Every time a new review is posted on Google, Yelp, or TripAdvisor, the system flags it, classifies the sentiment, and drafts a personalized response…
steps: Every time a new review is posted on Google, Yelp, or TripAdvisor, the system flags it, classifies the sentiment, and drafts a personalized response for the owner to approve and post, with negative reviews routed immediately to a priority inbox rather than sitting unnoticed for days.
Over time, the system tracks rating trends and identifies the most common complaint themes so the owner can address root causes rather than just managing one bad review at a time.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a restaurant owner has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Staff Scheduling & Open-Shift Fill System
automations.summary: When a team member calls out or a shift goes uncovered, the system automatically texts qualified, available staff in seniority order until someone…
steps: When a team member calls out or a shift goes uncovered, the system automatically texts qualified, available staff in seniority order until someone confirms coverage, then updates the schedule in real time and notifies the manager.
Scheduling for the upcoming week is drafted automatically based on historical sales volume by day and time, so the manager starts from a smart baseline rather than a blank spreadsheet every week.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a restaurant manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Scheduling software (e.g., 7shifts or When I Work)

automations.title: Event Inquiry & Banquet Event Order (BEO) Generator
automations.summary: Catering inquiries submitted via the website are automatically qualified (guest count, date, event type, budget) and the system generates a…
steps: Catering inquiries submitted via the website are automatically qualified (guest count, date, event type, budget) and the system generates a preliminary quote and schedules a discovery call on the events manager's calendar.

Once the event is confirmed and details are finalized, the BEO document is automatically assembled from the collected information and sent to the client for review and signature, eliminating hours of back-and-forth and manual document formatting.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a catering & events manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Inventory Count & Par-Level Reorder System
automations.summary: Weekly inventory counts submitted by bar staff through a simple mobile form are automatically compared against par levels set for each product, and…
steps: Weekly inventory counts submitted by bar staff through a simple mobile form are automatically compared against par levels set for each product, and any item below threshold generates a purchase order to the appropriate distributor or supplier.

The bar manager gets a single consolidated order sheet rather than rebuilding it from scratch every week, and the system tracks cost-per-pour trends over time to flag when a product's margin is slipping before it shows up in the P&L.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a bar manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Jotform or Google Forms (inventory count form)
Google Sheets or Airtable (par level database)

automations.title: Daily Location Announcement & Pre-Order System
automations.summary: Each morning, the owner confirms the day's location in a simple form, and the system automatically posts it to Facebook, Instagram, and Google…
steps: Each morning, the owner confirms the day's location in a simple form, and the system automatically posts it to Facebook, Instagram, and Google Business, sends a text blast to the VIP customer list, and opens a pre-order window for pickup so customers can order ahead from wherever they are.
The result is a ready line of customers when the truck arrives, higher per-location revenue, and a growing follower base that never has to wonder where the truck is today.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a food truck owner is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Reservation Confirmation & No-Show Reducer
automations.summary: The moment a guest books a table online or by phone, the system logs it in the reservation platform and immediately sends a text confirmation with…
steps: The moment a guest books a table online or by phone, the system logs it in the reservation platform and immediately sends a text confirmation with the date, time, and party size.

A reminder text goes out 24 hours before the reservation asking the guest to reply "C" to confirm or "X" to cancel, and a second, shorter reminder fires two hours before the seating window for same-day bookings.

Guests who don't respond to the 24-hour reminder are automatically called by a staff member the next morning instead of being left to guess, and no-show rates that used to run near 15-20% on weekend nights drop into the single digits once guests know a real person is tracking whether they show up.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a reservations manager is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Text-Based Waitlist & Table-Ready Alerts
automations.summary: Guests join the waitlist at the host stand or by scanning a QR code from the sidewalk, entering their name, party size, and phone number instead of…
steps: Guests join the waitlist at the host stand or by scanning a QR code from the sidewalk, entering their name, party size, and phone number instead of waiting for a buzzer or straining to hear their name called over restaurant noise.
As tables turn, the host taps "next" and the guest gets an automatic text letting them know their table is ready, with a second text sent if they don't check in within five minutes.

Wait time estimates update automatically based on how quickly parties ahead of them are actually being seated, not a fixed 20-minute guess, so guests can step away instead of crowding the entryway, and hosts spend far less time answering "how much longer" every ninety seconds.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a host stand lead remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Waitlist platform (e.g., Yelp Waitlist or NoWait)
POS system (e.g., Toast) for table status

automations.title: Post-Visit Review Funnel & Feedback Router
automations.summary: When the POS detects a closed check, the system waits two hours, then sends the guest a text or email asking one simple question: how was your visit?
steps: When the POS detects a closed check, the system waits two hours, then sends the guest a text or email asking one simple question: how was your visit?

Guests who respond positively are automatically routed to a direct link to leave a Google or Yelp review, while guests who indicate anything less than great are routed instead to a private feedback form that lands directly in the general manager's inbox rather than a public review page.

The manager can respond to a dissatisfied guest the same day, often before they've even thought about posting anywhere, and the restaurant's public rating climbs because only the genuinely happy visits get funneled toward public platforms.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a general manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Google Business Profile and Yelp Fusion API (review links)

automations.title: Instant Catering Inquiry Auto-Quote System
automations.summary: A catering inquiry submitted through the website form, guest count, event date, menu preferences, is instantly parsed and matched against a standing…
steps: A catering inquiry submitted through the website form, guest count, event date, menu preferences, is instantly parsed and matched against a standing per-head pricing sheet, generating a starter quote with two or three available date options sent back to the prospect within minutes instead of the next business day.
The coordinator is notified immediately with the full inquiry details and a draft quote already attached, ready to refine rather than build from scratch.

Catering leads often request quotes from three competitors at once, so being the first to respond with real numbers, sometimes within five minutes of submission, has meaningfully increased the percentage of inquiries that turn into booked events.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a catering sales coordinator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Slow-Night Demand Trigger & Promo Blast
automations.summary: The system checks reservation volume for each upcoming night against a rolling average for that day of the week, and when bookings for, say, a…
steps: The system checks reservation volume for each upcoming night against a rolling average for that day of the week, and when bookings for, say, a Tuesday fall more than 30% below normal with less than 48 hours to go, it automatically triggers a promo, a discount code or a limited-time offer, pushed out as an email and text to the restaurant's guest list.

The offer is capped at a set number of redemptions so it doesn't cannibalize a night that ends up busy anyway, and results (redemptions, covers seated, revenue) are logged automatically so the coordinator can see which offers actually fill seats.
Slow Tuesdays that used to just be accepted as slow now regularly close within 10-15% of a normal night's covers.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a marketing coordinator remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Birthday Club Auto-Offer System
automations.summary: Birthdays collected at checkout, on receipts, through a loyalty app, or via a simple sign-up form, feed automatically into a guest database, and on…
steps: Birthdays collected at checkout, on receipts, through a loyalty app, or via a simple sign-up form, feed automatically into a guest database, and on the first of each month every guest with a birthday that month receives an email with a free dessert or appetizer offer valid any time during their birthday month.
Guests who don't redeem within the first two weeks get a friendly reminder text with the offer attached again.

A free item redeemed almost always comes attached to a full paying party, so the birthday club consistently drives visits that wouldn't have happened that month otherwise, turning a single data field collected at checkout into a recurring, low-cost source of return traffic.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a guest relations manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: POS-Linked Ingredient Reorder Alerts
automations.summary: As menu items sell throughout the day, the POS deducts ingredient usage against a recipe-mapped inventory count, and once any ingredient's on-hand…
steps: As menu items sell throughout the day, the POS deducts ingredient usage against a recipe-mapped inventory count, and once any ingredient's on-hand quantity drops below its set par level, the system automatically emails a purchase order to the correct supplier with the standard order quantity pre-filled.

The kitchen manager gets a same-day notification of exactly what was ordered and from whom, and a weekly variance report flags ingredients being used faster than recipes predict, a signal of over-portioning or waste.
What used to be a Sunday-night ritual of counting walk-in shelves and phoning three different suppliers is now confirmed automatically before the manager finishes prep for the day.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a kitchen manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips.
tools: POS system (e.g., Toast or Square) with inventory module
Google Sheets or Airtable (par level database)

steps: Every morning, sales, labor percentage, average check, and covers from every location automatically roll up into a single digest emailed to ownership before the first location even opens for lunch, replacing the old routine of a multi-unit director manually logging into a separate POS dashboard for each address.

Locations trending outside their normal range on any metric are automatically highlighted at the top of the report, so a slipping location gets a phone call that same morning instead of the trend only becoming visible weeks later during a monthly review.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a multi-unit director, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: End-of-Shift Tip-Out Calculation Automation

steps: At the close of each shift, hours worked and role from the scheduling system are automatically matched against total tips collected in the POS, and the system calculates and allocates each employee's tip-out share according to the house's split rules, front-of-house, back-of-house, support staff, without a manager doing the math by hand at midnight.

A digital record of every calculation is stored automatically, giving the payroll administrator a clean audit trail if a dispute ever comes up, and closing out a shift now takes minutes instead of the error-prone spreadsheet math that used to keep managers at the restaurant long after the last table left.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a payroll administrator, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving.

steps: Marking a new hire as accepted in the scheduling system automatically triggers a sequence covering onboarding paperwork, a copy of the training schedule for their first two weeks, and a request to the kitchen or front-of-house lead for uniforms and system access to be ready before day one.

The HR onboarding coordinator no longer has to remember which of a dozen steps still needs doing for each new hire, since every task fires automatically off the same trigger, and new employees consistently show up to their first shift with a badge, a login, and a uniform waiting instead of standing around while someone scrambles to sort it out.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a hr onboarding coordinator remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips.
tools: Scheduling software (e.g., 7shifts or When I Work)

automations.title: Wine & Beverage Club Renewal Reminder

steps: Members of the wine or beverage club automatically receive a shipment notification and renewal reminder ahead of each billing cycle, along with the specific bottles or selections included in that period's shipment, instead of a charge simply appearing on a statement with no context.

Members whose card fails at renewal are automatically prompted to update their payment method before the club is paused, and the beverage director gets a monthly report of upcoming renewals, giving enough lead time to reach out personally to any member showing signs of churn before they cancel instead of after.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a beverage director has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Guest Allergy & Dietary Restriction Flagging System
automations.summary: When a guest notes an allergy or dietary restriction while booking online, the note is automatically attached to the reservation and pushed to both…
steps: When a guest notes an allergy or dietary restriction while booking online, the note is automatically attached to the reservation and pushed to both the kitchen and the assigned server ahead of the guest's arrival, so the issue is addressed proactively in the kitchen instead of being raised for the first time once the guest is already seated at the table.

Repeat guests with a restriction on file have it automatically carried forward to every future reservation, and the allergen safety coordinator gets a daily prep sheet listing every flagged guest coming in that shift, closing the gap between what a guest tells the host stand and what actually reaches the line.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, an allergen safety coordinator spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: New Review Response Speed Alert

steps: The instant a new review posts to Yelp or Google, the reputation specialist and the general manager automatically receive an alert with the review's star rating and full text, and anything under four stars is flagged as urgent so a thoughtful response can go out the same day instead of a review sitting unanswered for a week while a manager happens to check Yelp during a slow moment.

A drafted response option using the restaurant's own tone is generated automatically as a starting point, cutting response time down from days to hours and turning a public complaint into a visible example of the restaurant actually listening.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a reputation specialist, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Google Business Profile and Yelp Fusion API (review links)

steps: For dayparts that historically run quiet, an early lunch hour, a slow midweek happy hour, the system automatically sends a targeted promotion to nearby subscribers timed to land right before that window opens, driving traffic during the exact hours the restaurant most needs it rather than a generic discount blasted to everyone at the same time regardless of when they're likely to actually come in.

Redemption is tracked automatically by daypart, so the marketing coordinator can see over time which offers actually move covers during a specific window and retire the ones that don't, instead of running the same promotion indefinitely on a hunch.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a marketing coordinator spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

steps: Every delivered supplier invoice is automatically checked against the original purchase order line by line, and any mismatch in quantity or price is instantly flagged to the accounts payable coordinator before the invoice is approved for payment, instead of a discrepancy only surfacing weeks later during a full audit of the books.

Suppliers with recurring discrepancies are automatically tracked over time, giving management hard numbers to bring to a vendor conversation instead of a vague sense that a supplier's pricing "feels off," and the restaurant stops quietly overpaying for cases that were never actually delivered at the quoted price.

Enrollment through this moment converts at a far higher rate than enrollment prompted through a generic in-store sign or a QR code on a table tent, since it's timed to the exact moment a guest has just decided they enjoyed the experience enough to want a reason to come back.

Guests know the policy upfront when they book, and consistent, automatic enforcement means the fee actually deters no-shows the way it's meant to, rather than being unevenly applied only when someone remembers to follow through on it.

automations.summary: The automation monitors ratings specifically on third-party delivery platforms and flags a drop in delivery-only scores separately from dine-in…
